title: epics v1 — normalized artifact classification
description: The canonical object every carrier emits for one artifact (TODO item, commit, pull request, issue). One shape for all planes so aggregates never have to reconcile producer-specific vocabularies. `classification` is four-state on purpose: `epic: null` alone cannot distinguish a producer that never collected epics, a body read with no tag, a truncated body, and a parser failure.

epic.description: the epic exactly as written, after grammar validation; null unless classification is `tagged`

defect.description: optional defect class; orthogonal to the epic and never a substitute for it

diagnostics.description: ordered by (code, subject_key, subject_uri, related_uri) over raw Unicode code points, null sorting before any string — see the contract README's Canonicalization section

subject_uri.description: identity of the classified artifact; null only where the carrier has no addressable identity

carrier.description: which plane produced this classification — required, because per-plane completeness cannot be assembled from objects that may omit it

inherited_from.description: set when a commit's epic was inherited from its pull request (never derived from a `#123` subject reference)

observed_at.description: when the artifact was read (observation time, NOT activity time — see ADR-ECO-010 D11); required and nullable: a producer that does not stamp it must say so, not stay silent

resolved_from.description: set when a historical artifact carried a tombstoned id: `epic` holds the final id it resolves to, `resolved_from` the retired id as written. Aggregates stay single-valued; the retirement stays visible.

EpicId.description: always two levels, exactly one dot; the program prefix is part of the identity

ClassificationState.description: tagged = read and valid; missing = read, no epic; invalid = read, epic unusable; unavailable = not read. `unavailable` is never counted as `missing`.

ArtifactUri.description: todo://<repo>/<id> for plan items; git://<repo>/<sha> for commits; gh://<repo>/pull/<n> and gh://<repo>/issues/<n> for GitHub artifacts

severity.description: the COMPUTED severity for this instance; diagnostics.yaml states the policy that computes it

related_uri.description: the second artifact of a cross-plane finding (EP-CONFLICT)

raw.description: the offending value exactly as written, so a grammar diagnostic never loses the original

subject_key.description: the registry key a registry-scope finding is about (an epic id or a program id); artifact-scope findings leave it null and use subject_uri
